_comment: Minecraft version capability table. THE RULE FOR THIS FILE: no value is written from
memory. A row ships only when its numbers were read out of a real generated world or
a real pack, and `verified_from` records where. A wrong data_version produces a world
that loads and then quietly misbehaves, which is the worst failure mode we have.
To add a version: generate or open a world in it, read Data.Version.Name and
Data.Version.Id out of level.dat, and paste them here with the path you read.
BETTER SOURCE (used for the rows added 2026-08-09): every Minecraft client jar carries
`version.json` at its root, holding Mojang's own numbers for that release:
{ "id": "26.2", "world_version": 4903,
"pack_version": { "data_major": 107, "data_minor": 1, ... } }
`world_version` IS the DataVersion stamped into chunks and `pack_version.data*` IS the
data pack format that version loads. Reading them out of the jar is exact and needs no
world. It was cross-checked against the rows verified earlier from real level.dat files
(1.21.5 -> 4325, 26.1.2 -> 4790 and format 101.1); they matched, so the method holds.
data_version    -> written into every chunk as DataVersion
extended_height -> min_y/height in dimension_type; 1.17+ only
chunk_layout    -> 'flat' = 1.18+ ; 'legacy' = pre-1.18 (a separate writer path)
datapack_schema -> which shape pack.mcmeta and dimension_type must take:
'legacy'  = 1.21.4-1.21.10 era: integer pack_format plus
supported_formats/min_format/max_format, and the
multi-overlay dimension_type tree;
'modern'  = 26.x era: DECIMAL pack_format/min_format/max_format
(e.g. 101.1) and the attributes/timelines schema.
Getting this wrong is not cosmetic: 26.1.2 rejects the legacy
metadata outright with 'Failed to read pack metadata' and the
world refuses to load.
datapack_format -> the decimal pack_format for a 'modern' row. Absent = we have not
verified one, and extended height is refused rather than guessed.
The bundled extended-height pack declares a format RANGE with overlays rather than
a single pack_format, and that envelope is known-good: it is what the fork has been
shipping. Emitted packs reuse it verbatim, so we never have to guess a per-version
pack_format. If a future version falls outside this range, the pack must be
re-verified against that version before the range is widened.
What the writer emits when the caller names no version. This is the value the fork
has always written (src/world_editor/java.rs), kept for byte-compatibility. Its
version LABEL is unverified -- it sits between 1.21.5 (4325) and 26.1.2 (4790) --
so it is deliberately not presented as a named version anywhere in the UI.

versions.note: Predates extended build height (1.17). Generation with a non-vanilla profile is refused.

versions.verified_from: version.json of the 1.21.11 client jar under ModrinthApp profile 'Vulkan Optimized', 2026-08-09
versions.datapack_format_verified_from: same version.json, pack_version.data_major/minor = 94/1 — inside the pack's overlay_attributes range (90-100)

versions.verified_from: level.dat of the RomaniaSMP server world, 2026-08-05
versions.datapack_format_verified_from: pack.mcmeta of collective-26.1.2-8.32.jar, a data pack the 26.1.2 client loads successfully (see logs/latest.log), 2026-08-06; re-confirmed by version.json of the 26.1.2 client jar (pack_version.data 101/1), 2026-08-09
